python3 - <<'PY'
import statistics

# Data from bulletins:
# FY 1941-1942: from 1948 bulletin (page 54)
# FY 1943-1947: cross-reference - use 1950 bulletin values (later publication = authoritative)
# FY 1948-1950: from 1950 bulletin (page 56)

# Values from the "Total paper money" column (in millions of dollars):
paper_money = {
    1941: 8932,    # 1948 bulletin
    1942: 11600,   # 1948 bulletin
    1943: 16492,   # both agree
    1944: 21438,   # both agree
    1945: 25511,   # 1950 bulletin (revised, 1948 had 25541)
    1946: 26945,   # both agree
    1947: 26942,   # both agree
    1948: 26182,   # 1950 bulletin (revised, 1948 had 26482)
    1949: 26034,   # 1950 bulletin only
    1950: 25661,   # 1950 bulletin only
}

x = [paper_money[y] for y in sorted(paper_money.keys())]
years = sorted(paper_money.keys())

print("FY Range:", years[0], "-", years[-1])
print("n =", len(x))
print("Data:", list(zip(years, x)))

n = len(x)
mean = statistics.mean(x)
s = statistics.stdev(x)  # sample stdev (n-1 denominator)
print(f"\nMean = {mean}")
print(f"Sample stdev (s) = {s}")

# Compute excess kurtosis using scipy formula
# g2 = ((n*(n+1))/((n-1)*(n-2)*(n-3))) * sum(((x-mean)/s)**4) - 3*(n-1)**2/((n-2)*(n-3))
# This is the unbiased sample Fisher excess kurtosis

try:
    from scipy.stats import kurtosis
    k = kurtosis(x, fisher=True, bias=False)
    print(f"\nScipy Fisher excess kurtosis (bias=False): {k}")
except ImportError:
    print("scipy not available, using manual formula")

# Manual computation for verification
m4_num = sum(((xi - mean) / s) ** 4 for xi in x)
kurt_manual = ((n * (n + 1)) / ((n - 1) * (n - 2) * (n - 3))) * m4_num - 3 * (n - 1)**2 / ((n - 2) * (n - 3))
print(f"Manual Fisher excess kurtosis: {kurt_manual}")

# Round to thousandths
result = round(kurt_manual, 3)
print(f"\nRounded to thousandths: {result}")
PY
